business_scope.primary_industry_name: Single-Origin Green Arabica Coffee Bean Container Distribution

meta_jurisdiction_context.note: Samoa does not currently have a comprehensive DTAA with major G20 jurisdictions; offshore international company regime applies statutory tax exemption.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2018; International Companies Act 2015; Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Directives; applicable UN Security Council sanctions regulations; beneficial ownership filing requirements pursuant to Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of each proposed director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or identity issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Samoa is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming commercial history and KYC status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution in forwarding jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each individual principal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of constitutional documents and certificate of incorporation for each corporate shareholder or member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant company registry or competent corporate authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney in favor of the approved Samoan registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the relevant jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficiaries, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, and Samoa domestic sanctions designations under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates; continuous monitoring is required during the business relationship. Any positive match or suspicious transaction must be reported to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit. Records must be maintained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Company Registry Name Reservation Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script, being standard English or Samoan characters. International Company names must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Corp', 'Incorporated', or 'Inc', or a prescribed abbreviation. Names must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name; transliteration into Samoan is permitted but the Directors must maintain one standardized Latin-script version for all official registry records.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant or registered agent may file a written administrative appeal to the Registrar at SIFA within 14 days of rejection notice, stating grounds and attaching the rejection letter. SIFA must determine the appeal within 14 working days. If the appeal is upheld, the name is reserved for a further 14 days. If rejected on final appeal, the applicant may submit a fresh name reservation application. Extension of an unreserved name may be requested before expiry for one further 30-day period, subject to SIFA fee. If no appeal or extension is filed, the name reverts to the common pool.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual mail-forwarding address alone is not acceptable. The International Company must maintain a registered office at the physical office of a licensed Samoa registered agent. The registered agent's address may serve as the statutory registered office and as the primary official correspondence point; no separate virtual office is permitted in substitution for the licensed agent physical office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 30% over a three-year period for a standard low-risk International Company with compliant UBO filings and a properly appointed registered agent. Likelihood increases materially upon any anomalous transaction, incomplete beneficial ownership response, or adverse regulatory trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), principally ss. 5-13 (incorporation and certificate of incorporation), ss. 14-18 (shares and capital), ss. 19-24 (registered office and registered agent), and ss. 25-30 (directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Declaration of Compliance, Notice of Registered Office, and Particulars of Directors and Secretary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or bank deposit is required; the company may issue a single share at no par value or nominal value in any currency, provided the issued share capital is fully described in the first board resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriber’s subscription for 1,000 ordinary shares of no par value at USD 1.00 each, fully paid, is approved and accepted, such shares constituting the initial issued capital. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office in Apia, Samoa, maintained at [address of licensed registered agent], is adopted as the Company’s statutory registered office under the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director Name] is appointed sole director and [Secretary Name] is appointed company secretary, each holding office for the initial term stated in the Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the director and secretary, jointly or severally, are authorized to register the Company, issue share certificates, open bank accounts, appoint licensed service providers, and take all incidental actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application in the prescribed form with the proposed company name and two alternatives. The Registrar checks the name against the International Companies Register and restricted words list. Upon approval, the Registrar issues a name clearance certificate valid for sixty days. Avoid names implying banking, trust, insurance, or government patronage unless a separate licence is obtained.
required_dossiers: Name Clearance Application Form
Proposed company name and two alternative names
Passport copy of the subscriber or licensed formation agent
Letter of engagement from a licensed trust and company service provider
Payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, respond in writing to the Registrar within five business days with a revised name or rely on an approved alternative name. An appeal lies to the Registrar under the International Companies Act 1987 for unreasonable refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa, acting on behalf of the subscriber; no filing with the Registrar at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English. The document must state the company name, proposed authorized share capital, registered office clause, restricted activities, and powers of directors. The subscriber signs each page and the execution page is witnessed or notarized. The consent of the initial director and secretary is also executed. The agent verifies identities and beneficial ownership as part of customer due diligence.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed)
Consent to act as director and secretary
Passport and proof of residential address of subscriber and ultimate beneficial owner
Reference letter or source of funds statement required by the agent
Registered agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Memorandum and Articles are found to contain typographical errors or non-compliant provisions, they may be amended by a Certificate of Amendment or re-executed before filing. Re-execution does not attract a government penalty if the defect is cured prior to submission to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Documents to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent lodges the executed Memorandum and Articles together with the Notice of Registered Office, Particulars of Directors and Secretary, Declaration of Compliance, and the name clearance certificate. The statutory filing fee is paid by wire transfer or cashier’s cheque to the MCIL trust account. The Registrar stamps the receipt and issues an acknowledgment with a provisional file number.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Declaration of Compliance signed by the subscriber or agent
Notice of Registered Office address in Samoa
Particulars of Directors and Secretary
Name Clearance Certificate
Statutory filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an enquiry or requisition, the agent must respond within fourteen days with corrected documents or additional information. Any fee shortfall is cured by wire payment to the MCIL account before the application is re-submitted. If the defect is a missing consent or notarization, a corrected consent must be re-executed and lodged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Registration Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registrar examines the submitted documents, verifies the name clearance, and, if in order, enters the company on the International Companies Register. The Registrar signs and seals the Certificate of Incorporation and returns certified copies of the Memorandum and Articles. No audit of minimum capital is performed because no minimum paid-up capital requirement applies.
required_dossiers: Acknowledgment of provisional file number
Registered agent acceptance letter for the registered office
Payment receipt evidencing settlement of all fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains clerical errors in the company name, date, or registered office, the agent must apply for administrative correction within five business days. The incorporation is effective as of the date endorsed on the Certificate of Incorporation, not the date of the underlying filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa; board of directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial director convenes the first board meeting or passes a unanimous written resolution. The board adopts the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, officer appointments, authority to open bank accounts, company seal, and share certificate issuance. The minutes or written resolution is entered in the company’s records maintained at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Consent to act as director and secretary
Register of directors, officers, and shareholders
Share register or register of allotment
Specimen share certificate
Company seal register if a seal is adopted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a valid quorum cannot be established, the meeting may be adjourned for forty-eight hours and reconvened with any one director present, or the board may act through a unanimous written resolution. Any omission in minutes is cured by a supplemental memorandum signed by all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Bank Account and Operational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Samoa; Samoa Quarantine Division, Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries; Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (if a physical storage premises is used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board passes a banking resolution authorizing specified officers to open USD or WST accounts, including SWIFT wire facilities and documentary letter of credit arrangements. The company applies for a plant import permit for green coffee beans from Samoa Quarantine Division. If a warehouse or storage premises is used, the company obtains an occupancy fire safety certificate. No domestic business licence is required for the offshore International Company except for purely administrative representation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and certified Memorandum and Articles
First Board Resolution and banking resolution
Passports, proof of address, and beneficial ownership declarations for signatories
Plant Import Permit application for green coffee seeds or beans
Fire Safety Certificate and structural load confirmation if warehouse storage is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries beneficial ownership or source of funds, provide a full ownership chart and bank reference within ten business days. If quarantine rejects the plant import permit due to incomplete phytosanitary documentation, submit an amended certificate from the exporting authority. If the Fire Safety Certificate is withheld, remedy the identified fire safety defects and re-inspect the premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None for offshore International Company distribution of green coffee beans; Samoa Quarantine Division, Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, exercises import/phyto-sanitary control, and the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority exercises premises safety control.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or manufacturing operating license is required for single-origin green coffee bean import and container distribution. A Plant Import Permit under the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries is the relevant operational instrument.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required for a category C non-processing distribution activity. If a green coffee warehouse or light-processing facility is later established, a waste registration or full EIA may become applicable under the Environment Act 2001 and Waste Management Regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No liquid process discharge, VOC emissions, or wastewater discharges are associated with containerized green coffee distribution. If onsite processing or washing is added, the operator must comply with MNRE discharge limits of BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 50 mg/L, and must implement particulate dust control measures to avoid nuisance emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required for any warehouse or storage premises under the Fire and Emergency Services Act 2007, including structural load inspection for stacked coffee sacks and clear exit pathways. Occupational clearance for workers is evidenced by a workplace safety inspection under the Samoa OSH framework if physical staffing is deployed; no civil defense certificate is required for an administrative-only registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa (MfR), Government of Samoa; Online tax portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws; International Company registry supervision: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Companies Office portal: https://www.companies.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Confirm offshore status: An International Company incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is not required to obtain a TIN for pure offshore trading. 2. If a TIN is nonetheless required (e.g., for a Samoa-currency bank account, domestic employer obligations, or voluntary VAGST registration), a licensed registered agent in Samoa must submit Form IR-01 (Taxpayer Registration Form) to the Ministry for Revenue, attaching: certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation and the Charter/Memorandum issued by the Registrar of International Companies; certificate of appointment of the registered agent; original power of attorney from the board of directors; proof of the Samoa registered office and registered agent consent; board resolution declaring intended business activities; passport copies and proof of residential address of directors and beneficial owners; commercial bank reference; and AML-KYC information. 3. The Ministry for Revenue verifies the application and issues a unique 9-digit TIN within 3 to 5 business days. 4. If the entity makes or intends to make taxable supplies of goods or services in Samoa with annual turnover equal to or exceeding SAT 100,000, the same registration form will also be treated as a VAGST registration application, and the MfR will issue the corresponding VAGST certificate of registration with a stated effective date.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election or any domestic entity classification election. An International Company is automatically tax-exempt on its worldwide offshore income: no income tax, no VAGST, no stamp duty, no gift or estate duty, and no exchange control on foreign currency transactions. The entity may voluntarily elect to register for VAGST, but such an election does not remove the income tax exemption. If the IC amends its constitutional documents and converts to a Domestic Company under the Companies Act 2017, it becomes subject to the ordinary Samoa income tax system and may become liable to VAGST on domestic turnover. Hybrid-mismatch elections are not available, as Samoa has not enacted OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid-entity rules. The MfR nonetheless applies substance and beneficial-ownership documentation standards when reviewing a tax-exempt IC's annual filing with the registered agent.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 100,000 (Samoa Tala) annual value of taxable supplies; compulsory registration is triggered in the month immediately following the month in which taxable turnover exceeds this threshold, while voluntary registration is permitted for businesses making taxable supplies below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, or API-based digital stamping regime is currently enforced in Samoa. Registered businesses may issue paper tax invoices or PDF e-tax invoices in accordance with the VAGST Act. VAGST returns may be filed electronically through the Ministry for Revenue's e-services portal. Fiscal control is exercised through desk audits, cross-matching of customs declarations, and periodic invoice review. No third-party fiscal device mandate applies to international trading companies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated under the VAGST Act 2003 where the goods are exported to a destination outside Samoa before the supplier issues the tax invoice or within 28 days after the date of supply, and the supplier retains full documentary evidence of physical export. A supply of services is zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply and the services are performed entirely outside Samoa. For specialty green coffee beans exported in containers, the goods must be physically shipped from Samoa under a customs-approved export declaration, sold to a buyer outside Samoa, and paid for by inward remittance from that non-resident buyer. An International Company trading offshore from Samoa does not normally enter the VAGST system; if the entity is voluntarily registered and makes a zero-rated export, it may claim a refund of input VAGST on purchases attributable to that export under section 23 of the VAGST Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs Service export entry or SAD-2), with green coffee beans classified under HS heading 0901.11
Bill of Lading (named ocean carrier, evidencing shipment from a Samoa port to a destination outside Samoa)
Inward Remittance Certificate (issued by a licensed Samoan bank showing receipt of hard-currency payment from the non-resident buyer)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (cross-referenced to the export declaration)
Certificate of Origin (issued by the Samoa Chamber of Commerce or Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade)
Container seal number and port-of-loading verification report
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: A false export zero-rating claim is subject to retrospective assessment at the standard VAGST rate (15%) on the under-declared export value, plus late payment penalty of 10% and accruing interest. For fraudulent or deliberately understated claims, the Ministry for Revenue may impose a civil penalty tax of up to 100% of the tax shortfall and, in the case of criminal prosecution, a fine not exceeding SAT 50,000 or imprisonment not exceeding two years, or both. Refunds already paid may be clawed back together with penalties where the supporting export documentation is false, forged, inconsistent with customs records, or where the inward remittance does not come from the stated offshore buyer within the 180-day benchmark. Officers of the International Company may be personally liable, and the registered agent may be directed by the Registrar to strike the company off the International Companies Register for non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), which exercises foreign exchange control powers under the Exchange Control Act 1977 and delegates day-to-day supervision and processing to authorized dealer commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoa Tala (WST) is a managed currency pegged to a trade-weighted basket comprising mainly the US Dollar, Australian Dollar, New Zealand Dollar and Euro. Current-account transactions, including documented trade payments for green coffee imports, are generally processed by authorized dealers without prior central bank approval, although the supporting commercial documentation must be retained. Capital-account transactions, including equity injections into and dividend or liquidation remittances out of an International Company, require exchange-control approval or deemed approval through the receiving authorized dealer; in practice, a fully compliant International Company with a licensed registered agent faces minimal material hurdles, but profit remittances are subject to evidence of audited financial statements and a written declaration that no Samoan domestic tax liability exists, given the tax-exempt status of International Companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Central Bank of Samoa Exchange Control Notices, all export proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa within three months from the date of shipment and 100% of such proceeds must be surrendered to an authorized dealer in Samoa Tala unless a specific foreign-currency retention approval has been granted for an approved account. For the specialty green coffee import and redistribution model, the International Company must submit a CBS trade declaration for each shipment, retain the authorized dealer's foreign-exchange settlement advice, and make the full transaction record available for examination for at least five years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and WST/USD Operational Account
Operational Account in WST and USD

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: International banking licensee operating under the Samoa International Financial Services Centre regime

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa's Exchange Control Act 1977 and Central Bank of Samoa licensing framework recognize only authorized dealers and licensed money-changers as lawful foreign-exchange intermediaries; offshore digital EMIs have no clearing equivalence for Samoa Tala transactions, cannot discharge the export-proceeds surrender obligation, and are not eligible to operate domestic payment or settlement rails in Samoa. An offshore EMI may be used only as a supplementary pre-funded US Dollar disbursement vehicle for supplier payments outside Samoa, never as the primary liquidity or compliance rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoan banks universally require at least one authorized signatory who is a natural-person director or an officer with board-approved signing authority to complete a face-to-face interview at the bank's Apia branch, or with a bank-approved agency representative physically located in the shareholder's home jurisdiction. Remote onboarding is permitted only for well-established BSP global customers or where the ultimate beneficial owner maintains a proven Commonwealth or APEC banking relationship, subject to enhanced due diligence consisting of a live video verification call, certified true copies of passports and proof of address, and notarized appointment documents for every corporate officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company registered in Samoa with 100% non-resident ownership and no local employees operating as an opaque offshore structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and current Statement of Good Standing from the Samoa Companies Registry; certified true copies of the Memorandum and Articles of Association; up-to-date Register of Directors and Shareholders; current certificate of appointment of the licensed Samoan registered agent; and a signed declaration of economic substance confirming that corporate administration is properly maintained by the Samoan registered agent and that the company engages exclusively in lawful commodity trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Green coffee trade flows routed through third-country brokers or consolidators in UAE, Singapore or Hong Kong, creating geographic-risk flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial contracts between the International Company and ultimate producers or licensed exporters; notarized supplier invoices showing the specific single-origin lot; bills of lading and airway bills demonstrating the physical routing of specialty green coffee; ISO 22000 and chain-of-custody certificates for the coffee lots; and complete USD correspondent-bank wiring trails confirming that each third-country intermediary is merely a payment and logistics conduit and never takes title to the underlying commodity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner resident in the People's Republic of China without a Samoan tax identification number and with ownership held through family holding structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized PRC public-security passport and second government-issued identification card; utility bill or property title as proof of address; business registration record of the Chinese operating parent or family holding vehicle; twelve months of shareholder bank statements as evidence of source of funds; a notarized source-of-wealth declaration; a private-client legal opinion from a cooperating law firm confirming the UBO is not a politically exposed person and is not subject to sanctions; and at least one bank reference letter from a tier-one Chinese trade-finance bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward equity injection spikes disproportionate to the International Company's filed memorandum capital and paid-up records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and shareholder resolutions authorizing the capital increase; certified bank statements of the remitting shareholder covering a twelve-month period; valuation certificate if the capital contribution takes the form of in-kind green coffee inventory; the stamped CBS capital-import declaration from the receiving authorized dealer; and the legal opinion confirming the capital is genuine equity rather than disguised third-party financing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward capital injections must be routed by wire through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the International Company's WST or USD account held at a Samoan authorized dealer, with the beneficiary field identifying the International Company and the remitting shareholder, and the purpose code mapped to BPM6 capital-account code 8M1 for equity capital in cash; the receiving authorized dealer must retain the board resolution, share certificate, and CBS capital-import declaration before crediting the funds to the capital escrow account, and any conversion into Samoa Tala occurs at the prevailing authorized-dealer buying rate with a permanent exchange-control record issued to the entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are executed through (i) SWIFT MT103 straight documentary payment against a sight purchase invoice for single-origin green coffee lots, and (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued by the Samoan authorized dealer under SWIFT MT700 in favor of the overseas supplier or producer; every outward payment must be supported by the purchase order, commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, phytosanitary and quality inspection certificate, and evidence of insurance, and the paying bank is required to apply full UN, OFAC and EU sanctions screening across the entire correspondent-bank chain, with the CBS purpose code recorded as ordinary merchandise trade in foodstuffs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contracts in WST/USD, WST/AUD, WST/EUR and WST/NZD with a Samoan authorized dealer, supported by 100% underlying coffee trade documentation and strict settlement on the maturity date.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the Samoa Tala executed through an offshore executing desk only where the Samoan authorized dealer confirms in writing that the instrument creates no enforceable onshore Tala liability and final settlement is in US Dollars against the IMF-recognized WST reference rate.

Cross-currency swaps between USD and WST in connection with long-term specialty green coffee supply agreements, subject to specific prior approval from the Central Bank of Samoa due to the maturity-mismatch nature of such trades.

Commodity price swap contracts fixing the green coffee differential against the C-Price benchmark, which are treated as documented OTC derivatives outside the foreign-exchange control regime and booked through a licensed commodity broker in a permissive jurisdiction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Renewal — Annual Government Licence Fee and Statutory Status Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation in each calendar year; any payment submitted after that date is treated as late and incurs a statutory late-renewal surcharge.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a statutory late-renewal surcharge. If the licence fee and surcharges remain unpaid after the Registrar issues the statutory strike-off notice, the company is liable to be struck off the International Companies Register and dissolved. Restoration requires a formal application, payment of all arrears, penalties and restoration fees, and is subject to the Registrar's discretion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Appointed Registered Agent and Samoa International Companies Registry through the registered agent's attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each annual renewal date and promptly after any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an accurate Register of Beneficial Owners is a statutory offence and may subject the company, its directors and the registered agent to financial penalties. Continued inaccuracy or unavailability of UBO records may cause the Registry to withhold the Certificate of Good Standing and institute administrative strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not applicable — a Samoa International Company has no compulsory statutory audit threshold. An audit is required only when voluntarily appointed by the board or members, imposed by a lender, requested by the registered agent under anti-money-laundering due diligence, or required by the jurisdiction in which the company carries on regulated business.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The International Companies Act 1987 does not prescribe IFRS or a domestic GAAP. The company must keep records sufficient to explain its financial position and every transaction. If accounts are voluntarily audited, IFRS or another internationally accepted accounting framework may be adopted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must hold a Register of Beneficial Owners in Samoa at its registered office. The registered agent must verify the identity of all ultimate beneficial owners, record any transfer or change of ownership, and provide an annual attestation to the Registry that the UBO register is complete and current. A share transfer can be registered only after the board approves the transfer and the registered agent updates the UBO register accordingly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners / UBO Register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0 if no audit is required; US$1,500 – US$5,000 per engagement if a voluntary certified audit is arranged

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Samoa International Company (IC) is statutorily classified as a tax-exempt offshore entity under the International Companies Act 1987. All income derived from outside Samoa, including international containerized distribution and trading profits of single-origin green Arabica coffee beans, is wholly exempt from Samoa corporate income tax. The effective Samoa CIT rate for a qualifying non-resident IC is therefore 0%, provided no Samoa-source activity is undertaken. The IC instead pays a fixed annual government fee via its licensed registered agent. Preferential tax holiday status: full statutory CIT exemption for all offshore-source profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return of an International Company (Form IC-AR) filed with the Registrar of International Companies through the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Companies Online Registry, submitted by the licensed Samoa registered agent. No corporate income tax return is lodged if the IC remains exclusively offshore.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation, together with payment of the annual government fee. If the IC fails to certify its offshore-exclusive status, a corporate income tax return must instead be filed within 6 months of the financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC full legal name, registration number, incorporation date, registered office in Samoa, and the name and licence number of the Samoa registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners are not required to disclose residential addresses on the public register, but the registered agent must hold verified proof of identity and physical global address for its client file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B - Share Capital and Shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized capital, issued share classes, number of issued shares, and registered shareholder names.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident individual and corporate shareholders are permitted. Nominee shareholders are allowed provided the beneficial owner is separately disclosed to the registered agent and the Financial Intelligence Unit upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, nationalities, occupation, and residential addresses of all directors and the corporate secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: At least one director is mandatory; non-resident directors are fully permitted and no Samoa physical residency requirement applies for directors of an International Company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part D - Business Activity and Offshore Source Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that the IC carries on business exclusively outside Samoa and derives no Samoa-source income; description of principal activity as international green coffee bean distribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must certify that no warehousing, repacking, grading, or sale of coffee occurs in Samoa. Any incidental storage in Samoa creates a domestic-source apportionment and requires immediate written notice to the Ministry of Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Natural person or persons holding more than 25% of shares or voting rights, including full legal name, date of birth, and nationality.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The beneficial ownership schedule is filed confidentially and is not part of the public registry. Non-resident beneficial owners with controlling interest in the Samoa IC must be accurately identified or the filing is deemed unlawful.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form IC-AR attracts a late fee of WS$50 plus WS$10 for each day of delay up to a maximum of WS$250. Failure to pay the annual government fee for two consecutive years results in administrative striking-off. A knowingly false offshore certification triggers income tax evasion penalties under the Income Tax Act 2015, including a penalty of up to 100% of any tax understated, interest of 2% per month, and the reversal of the IC tax exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CIT-1) lodged electronically on the Samoa Ministry of Revenue Online Taxpayer Portal. This return is mandatory only in the exceptional case where an International Company has derived Samoa-source income, failed to maintain its offshore status, or carried on business in Samoa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Under the Income Tax Act 2015, the annual CIT return is due within 6 months after the end of the financial year. A 3-month extended filing window is available upon written application to the Ministry of Revenue before the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income assessable in Samoa, including Samoa-source trading, service, storage, and distribution income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC, only income sourced in Samoa is declared; offshore green coffee export and international container freight profits are excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income exempt under the International Companies Act 1987 and Income Tax Act 2015, specifically all foreign-derived trading and distribution profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IC must attach a detailed schedule identifying counterparties, container volumes, routes from origin port to destination port, and evidence that no Samoa-source intervention occurred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenditure wholly and exclusively incurred in producing assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs may deduct direct procurement costs, logistics, freight, insurance, inspection, and documented agency fees, but no deduction is available for management fees paid to offshore principals unless supported by an arm-length transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated taxable income upon which the 27% statutory corporate tax rate applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the IC has inadvertently triggered Samoa residence, the taxable amount is limited to Samoa-source revenues less attributable deductions; proper transfer pricing analysis is required for imported green coffee cost of goods sold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Credits and Withholding Tax Set-off
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and Samoan withholding tax credits claimed against the computed corporate tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs may apply treaty credits only where a Samoa DTA is in force; all claims require a validated Tax Residence Certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of total corporate tax due, increasing to 25% if the default exceeds 30 days, plus a daily surcharge of 2% of unpaid tax during continued default. Wilful omission of Samoa-source coffee trading income may elevate the matter to criminal tax evasion with fines up to WS$1,000,000 and imprisonment, alongside reinstatement of the 27% CIT over a 5-year audit period.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on dividends paid by a Samoa resident company to a non-resident shareholder. Zero withholding applies to dividend distributions from an exempt International Company funded exclusively by offshore profits, as the distribution is outside the Samoa tax net.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa maintains comprehensive double taxation agreements with Australia and New Zealand, and negotiates further Pacific regional agreements. To invoke treaty relief on any Samoan-source payment, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a completed DTA relief claim form to the Samoan payer, accompanied by an original Samoa Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the Ministry of Revenue, together with a declaration of beneficial ownership, no later than the payment date or within the statutory refund window. Since a tax-exempt IC pays no Samoa CIT, no TRC is sought in the ordinary course; instead, a Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Registrar of International Companies is used to evidence the IC's tax-exempt status before foreign tax authorities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest paid by a Samoa resident to a non-resident is 15%; statutory withholding on royalties is also 15%. Under the Samoa-Australia and Samoa-New Zealand DTAs, the withholding may be reduced to 10% for interest and 5% for royalties, subject to full beneficial ownership certification and submission of the TRC. For an exempt International Company, no Samoan withholding is imposed on offshore royalty or interest flows, and coffee brand or distribution royalties paid by the IC to foreign principals are not taxable in Samoa.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa law does not publish a statutory tala threshold, but the administrative benchmark triggering mandatory transfer pricing documentation, including Local File and Master File, is aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceeding WS$5,000,000 per income year. For transactions above WS$1,000,000, the Ministry of Revenue may compel contemporaneous documentation. The specialty green coffee IC should retain at the registered agent's office a full Local File whenever related-party coffee purchases exceed WS$5,000,000 or when the IC sells to a foreign affiliate of the ultimate beneficial owner.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019 apply mandatory economic substance requirements to Samoa International Companies conducting relevant activities. Coffee container distribution by a Samoa IC falls within the distribution and service centre definition where inventory is procured from or sold to associated enterprises. The IC must demonstrate: (a) physical office or dedicated business premises in Samoa; (b) full-time qualified employees engaged in the coffee logistics and distribution management; (c) board meetings and senior management decisions occurring in Samoa; (d) adequate operational expenditure in Samoa. An annual Economic Substance Declaration must be filed through the registered agent. A purely pass-through offshore trading conduit that lacks local substance is non-compliant and may be struck off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An International Company certifies exclusive offshore business activity in its Annual Return while actually conducting Samoa domestic coffee distribution, storing green coffee containers in Samoa, or sourcing profits from a Samoan buyer without filing a Samoa CIT return and withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive loss of tax-exempt status; reassessment of all Samoa-source income at 27% corporate tax; evasion penalty of up to 100% of tax understated; interest at 2% per month; administrative strike-off from the Registry; publication of the IC as a non-compliant entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certified false offshore status are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax through judicial piercing of the corporate veil, with civil restitution, freezing of personal assets, travel restraint orders, and imprisonment of up to 7 years for fraudulent tax conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Deficient Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox entity with no Samoa board control, no local employees, no premises, and no Economic Substance Declaration while carrying on cross-border green coffee distribution with the benefit of the Samoa IC zero-tax regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic substance penalties of up to WS$1,000,000; cancellation of the IC registration; automatic exchange of information to the ultimate parent's foreign tax authority under Samoa's exchange-of-information network; foreign recharacterization of the Samoan IC as a transparent shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal civil restitution of government penalties, disqualification from holding any corporate office in Samoa for up to 10 years, and travel bans imposed by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit pending completion of the substance investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain an adequate beneficial ownership register, use of bearer shares, concealment of the controlling principal of the specialty coffee supply chain, or receipt of container settlement proceeds from an unvetted counterparty without assessing AML risk and filing a Suspicious Activity Report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines up to WS$500,000; registered agent licence suspension; forfeiture of the IC's bank balances; mandatory deregistration and referral to the Public Prosecutor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors convicted of money laundering face imprisonment of 5 to 10 years, monetary penalties of up to three times the laundered amount, personal travel bans, and disqualification under the Samoa AML/CFT Act 2018.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Striking-Off for Non-Filing of Annual Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the IC Annual Return and pay the annual government fee for two consecutive years while the coffee container trading activities continue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative striking-off of the International Company; all undischarged IC assets vest in the financial authority; late surcharges and restoration fees; loss of limited liability protection for post-striking-off contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Former directors remain personally liable for debts contracted after striking-off and may be prohibited from re-registering any International Company in Samoa for 5 years, with potential contempt sanctions for using the struck-off entity to settle coffee trade obligations.
